papers.title: An In-Ear Sleep Modulation SoC Featuring a CNN-LSTM Accelerator with Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Runtime Dynamic Quantization.
papers.journal: Digest of technical papers. Symposium on VLSI Technology
papers.summary: The work presents a 65 nm system-on-chip for closed-loop in-ear sleep modulation that performs low-noise in-ear EEG sensing, CNN-LSTM-based sleep stage classification, and phase-specific auditory stimulation under 1 mW. A dedicated accelerator with long-kernel memory reuse and runtime dynamic quantization reduced model size by 3.88× with only 0.28% accuracy loss, achieving 98.3% sensitivity for deep sleep detection.

papers.title: Measuring excitation/inhibition balance through field potentials
papers.summary: Using single-unit and LFP recordings from rat medial prefrontal/orbitofrontal cortex and mouse visual cortex/hippocampus, the study evaluated four EEG-based metrics against empirically measured excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance. Broadband (6-80 Hz) and high gamma (80-150 Hz) power consistently correlated with E/I, and broadband power from at least 30 minutes of medial prefrontal cortex data could rank animals by E/I ratio.

papers.title: When More Is Not Better: Component Anti-Synergy in a P300 Speller
papers.summary: The paper tested whether combining individually promising components in a P300 speller is additive using a four-component full-factorial experiment varying Euclidean Alignment, xDAWN spatial filtering, subject calibration, and language model priors on a public dataset. Results showed that component value is conditional rather than additive, with calibration the strongest singular contributor, anti-synergy between components, and language model support not universally beneficial.

papers.title: Interpretable self-supervised transformers for resting-state EEG analysis in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: The paper introduces STT-EEG, a self-supervised spatio-temporal transformer for early Alzheimer's disease detection from resting-state EEG. It achieved 96.42% accuracy for AD vs. CN classification and a Pearson correlation of 0.872 for MMSE prediction, with self-supervised pretraining contributing the largest ablation improvement (+7.08%).

papers.title: A meta-analysis of periodic and aperiodic electrophysiological features in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis of open-access M/EEG datasets (6 datasets; 368 Parkinson's patients, 570 controls) compared periodic and aperiodic resting-state features. Parkinson's patients showed elevated aperiodic exponent and offset, higher unadjusted beta power that disappeared after aperiodic adjustment, higher alpha power, and slower alpha peak frequency.

papers.title: pyAvalanches: A Python Package for Analyzing Spatiotemporal Propagation in Neuronal Avalanches
papers.summary: The paper introduces pyAvalanches, an open-source Python package providing a standardized end-to-end pipeline for neuronal avalanche analysis from electrophysiological recordings, with core innovation in computing Avalanche Transition Matrices to map spatiotemporal propagation patterns and derive network-based metrics. It demonstrates utility through group-level analysis of a public resting-state EEG dataset comparing propagation patterns across clinical populations.

papers.title: A unified signal-quality assessment framework for synchronized electro-intravascular encephalography and scalp electroencephalography.
papers.summary: The authors proposed a unified signal-quality assessment framework for electro-intravascular encephalography (EiEG) and validated it in an ovine model with a stent-mounted electrode in the superior sagittal sinus, synchronously recorded with scalp EEG. EiEG showed high physiological concordance (Spearman's ρ>0.94), higher linear SNR (2.04 vs Cz, 1.84 vs C1), and greater across-bout consistency (CV 0.8% vs 29.8% for Cz and 6.7% for C1) than scalp EEG.

papers.title: Predicting Speech in Noise Perception using Measures of Neural Entrainment
papers.summary: EEG data from 25 young healthy listeners performing speech-in-noise tasks were used to train temporal response function (TRF) models with speech envelope and gammatone spectrogram regressors. Neural entrainment to the attended stimulus positively predicted speech-in-noise performance, while entrainment to the unattended stimulus negatively predicted performance, and the difference between attended and unattended correlation coefficients was also significantly related to better performance.

papers.title: Scale-Dependent Development of Neural Signal Complexity and its Association with Working Memory in Childhood.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG from 253 typically developing children aged 3–9 years was analyzed using modified multiscale entropy (mMSE) across 20 temporal scales. Neural signal complexity increased with age in a scale-dependent and region-specific manner, and regional mMSE values were positively associated with short-term working memory capacity in frontal, occipital, and temporal regions.

papers.title: Reduced dynamical variability in depression: evidence from EEG and QIF-E network simulation.
authors: Thaise Graziele L de O Toutain
papers.summary: The study compared EEG complexity in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) patients and healthy controls using multiscale entropy (MSE), finding higher mean entropy at broader time scales and reduced inter-individual variability in MDD. Simulations with a Quadratic Integrate-and-Fire network showed that configurations lacking local electrical coupling reproduced key MDD entropy features, suggesting that local coupling structure modulates complexity-variability balance.

papers.title: Age-related hyperexcitability in the mouse inferior colliculus: evidence from sound-evoked local field potentials
papers.summary: The study assessed age-related changes in sound-evoked local field potentials (LFPs) across the tonotopic axis of the mouse inferior colliculus. It found significant age-related hyperexcitability in medial and dorsal regions, with oldest old animals showing enhanced N1 amplitudes and level-dependent spectral power changes, while ventral regions were unaffected.

papers.title: Separable Codes for Time and Decision in Human Temporal Perception
papers.summary: Thirty human participants performed a temporal discrimination task while EEG was recorded, and multivariate pattern analysis dissociated neural representations of physical duration and categorical decision. Both duration and category information were encoded throughout the trial with distinct temporal profiles along separable neural dimensions, and an Internal Reference Model indicated dynamic updating of internal references.

papers.title: What Static Connectivity Misses: Dynamic Alpha-Band Brain Network States in First-Episode Psychosis.
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG alpha-band connectivity was analyzed in 78 first-episode psychosis (FEP) individuals and 60 healthy controls using both static graph theory and dynamic connectivity clustering into five brain network states (BNS). Dynamic metrics revealed reduced variability in characteristic path length within a default mode network-associated BNS in FEP, and BNS metrics correlated with social cognition in controls and positive formal thought disorder in FEP, whereas static metrics showed no such associations.

papers.title: Clinical utility of in-ear EEG electrodes in hospitalized patients: comparison with standard scalp EEG.
papers.summary: The study evaluated in-ear EEG against standard scalp EEG in 30 hospitalized patients, finding 83.3% sensitivity, 80.0% specificity, and 82.8% accuracy for detecting neurophysiological abnormalities, with substantial agreement for encephalopathy grading. In-ear EEG was well-suited for diffuse dysfunction but missed one focal seizure, indicating reduced spatial coverage.

papers.title: Cortical Network Reorganization During Balance Control in Chronic Stroke: Premotor-Parietal Behavioral Uncoupling and Directional Prefrontal Compensation.
papers.summary: Cortical functional connectivity was measured with EEG during a balance task in 15 chronic stroke survivors and 15 matched healthy adults. Stroke participants showed elevated gamma-band connectivity from SMA-PM to PCC, ipsilesional LPFC to SMA-PM, and SMA-PM to contralesional LPFC; stronger SMA-PM to contralesional LPFC connectivity was associated with better Berg Balance Scale scores, suggesting compensatory prefrontal recruitment.

papers.title: Brain dynamics and creativity: Investigating the relationship between 1/f patterns of the resting-state EEG and divergent thinking.
papers.summary: In N=91 participants, resting-state EEG was decomposed with FOOOF, and latent associations between periodic alpha, aperiodic exponent, and divergent thinking/working memory were tested. Alpha power was positively associated with working memory in both eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions, while aperiodic exponent and alpha showed only non-significant trends with divergent-thinking fluency and no reliable associations with originality.

papers.title: During natural vision, semantic novelty modulates fixation-related processing in primate cortex
papers.summary: Fixation-related potentials and intracranial high-frequency activity were recorded in humans and macaques during natural movie viewing to test whether semantic novelty across saccades modulates visual processing. Only semantic novelty, not low- or mid-level novelty, modulated frontal and occipital fixation-related potentials in scalp EEG and broadband high-frequency activity in ventral visual and frontal areas, with stronger effects for movies than static images and early frontal modulation suggesting top-down integration.

papers.title: Interpretable AI for neural signal decoding in dementia: an EEG ensemble approach to differential diagnosis.
papers.summary: The study developed an interpretable ensemble machine learning framework using EEG features from resting-state and photic stimulation to differentiate Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia, achieving 95.63% accuracy on a held-out test set. SHAP analysis identified beta-band hemispheric asymmetry and alpha-band reactivity as key discriminative features.

papers.title: Preserved cue-state recruitment but prolonged preparatory activity in developmental dyscalculia.
papers.summary: Cue-locked EEG was recorded from 143 children during a conditional numerical Go/No-Go task to examine preparatory state recruitment in developmental dyscalculia (DD). Both DD and typically developing children showed a similar broad posterior-positive preparation pattern, but DD exhibited prolonged late expression of the preparatory state (448–798 ms) with later temporal centroid and peak, indicating altered temporal regulation rather than failed cue detection or rule recruitment.

papers.title: Distinct roles of brain network flexibility in motor learning across age.
papers.summary: EEG study of younger and older adults during a visuomotor learning task found that the learning aftereffect was associated with brain network flexibility during motor preparation in younger adults, but this association was absent in older adults.

papers.title: Dissociating the hierarchical processing of perceptual and food category information under different task demands.
papers.summary: EEG data from participants performing perceptual (color-matching) or categorical (food/nonfood) one-back tasks were analyzed with multivariate pattern analysis and cross-task representational similarity analysis to dissociate perceptual and food category processing. Perceptual features dominated early (100–200 ms), food category information emerged around 120 ms and became dominant after 200 ms, with selective enhancement of category information in late windows under the categorical task, demonstrating independent food category representations not reducible to low-level perceptual features.

papers.title: Uncovering the representational geometry of durations
papers.summary: Using behavioural similarity judgments and EEG oddball detection, the authors constructed representational dissimilarity matrices and found that duration representation is best explained by three latent dimensions (magnitude, contextual encoding, periodic component) consistent with a generalized helical model, with neural geometry showing logarithmic encoding around 150 ms and spring-like geometry around 300 ms after offset.

papers.title: Answer-locked ERP dynamics during arithmetic verification in children with developmental dyscalculia.
papers.summary: This study used an answer-locked ERP design to compare neural dynamics during arithmetic verification in 76 children (37 with developmental dyscalculia, 39 typically developing). Children with DD showed longer N2a and N2b peak latencies and smaller P3 amplitude at frontal sites, indicating delayed early processing and reduced later frontal activity during arithmetic verification.

papers.title: MRI-informed multi-modal deep learning for EEG source imaging with subject-specific head structure recognition.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: The authors developed a subject-specific multi-modal deep learning framework for EEG source imaging that integrates temporal EEG with structural MRI-derived head models. In simulation it achieved 5 mm localization error at 1.64 ms inference, outperforming conventional inverse methods, deep learning baselines, and a uni-modal EEG-only model, with preserved advantages on intracranial-stimulation data.

papers.title: Respiration-action coupling generalizes across distinct finger movement configurations.
papers.summary: Participants performed self-paced finger movements varying in muscle recruitment and direction while EEG and respiration were recorded. Movement onsets clustered in mid-to-late expiration across all conditions, readiness potential (RP) waveforms did not differ by movement type, and RP amplitude was larger during expiration than inspiration, indicating that respiration-action coupling generalizes across movement configurations.

papers.title: Retrieval practice prevents stress-induced inference impairment and preserves rapid bridge-related memory reactivation
papers.summary: Acute stress impaired A-C inference accuracy and speed and disrupted rapid EEG reactivation of bridge element B, while retrieval practice buffered these stress effects and enhanced bridge reactivation beyond the non-stress condition.

papers.title: Digital twins in dementia: Early evidence and future directions for precision psychiatry.
papers.summary: This review summarizes 20 studies (2015–2025) on digital twin applications in dementia across diagnosis, care, drug discovery, and computational modeling. Findings suggest promise in drug discovery and early detection via EEG/neuroimaging twins, but clinical validation and ethical frameworks remain limited.

papers.title: Reduced Motor Preparation and Altered EEG Signatures of Prediction in Autistic Adults.
papers.summary: Autistic adults showed less behavioral benefit from high-probability cues and reduced late CNV, altered mu/beta desynchronization, and weaker 1 Hz neural entrainment, implicating reduced motor preparation and altered prediction in autism.

papers.title: Differentially Private EEG Feature Anonymization: A Privacy-Utility Case Study in Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Studied differential privacy (DP) for clinical EEG feature anonymization using Gaussian and Laplace perturbations across client-side, centralized, and decentralized deployment scenarios. Found that the choice of mechanism, privacy parameters, and sensitivity calibration strongly influenced data utility, highlighting a practical privacy-utility trade-off in small, imbalanced clinical EEG datasets.

papers.title: Hikikomori symptoms, depressive symptoms, and frontal beta activity in young adult males with gaming disorder.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 59 males with gaming disorder and age-matched healthy controls, hierarchical logistic regression showed depressive symptoms and hikikomori total symptoms (specifically the physical isolation subscale) were independently associated with gaming disorder, whereas resilience was not. Resting-state EEG did not differ between groups; within the gaming disorder group, nominally higher frontal beta activity at Fz, F3, and F4 in the high-hikikomori subgroup was attenuated after adjustment for depressive symptoms, suggesting frontal beta power reflects overlapping depressive and social withdrawal burden rather than a hikikomori-specific biomarker.

papers.title: Heartfulness Meditation-induced State and Trait Effects on Long-term, Short-term and Non-meditators Using Connectivity Analysis: An EEG Study on Prefrontal Cortex.
papers.summary: Assessed Heartfulness meditation's state and trait effects on prefrontal EEG connectivity and graph-theoretic measures in long-term meditators, short-term meditators, and non-meditators across baseline, meditation, transmission, and post-transmission states. Found improved coordination, increased global and local efficiency (state effect), and significant trait changes in long-term meditators in delta, theta, and alpha bands.

papers.title: Neural correlates of response inhibition following cognitive behavioral therapy in obsessive-compulsive disorder: a randomized controlled EEG study.
papers.summary: Randomized controlled trial examining whether 12-week CBT with exposure and response prevention alters behavioral and electrophysiological indices of response inhibition in 60 adults with OCD. Found that CBT significantly reduced OCD symptom severity, increased No-Go P3 amplitude (Group × Time interaction), and reduced commission errors compared to a waitlist control.

papers.title: Facial palsy reveals the sensorimotor contribution to facial-emotion recognition.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: The paper tests an ambiguity-gated, developmentally calibrated architecture for facial-emotion recognition by studying neurotypical adults and individuals with congenital (Moebius syndrome) or acquired facial palsy. It found severity-performance coupling for nonprototypical expressions in both palsy cohorts, and for prototypical expressions only in the Moebius cohort, with reduced sensorimotor-face-network connectivity in Moebius.

papers.title: Biomarkers for mood disorders: A scoping review of research from India.
papers.summary: This scoping review synthesizes 56 Indian biomarker studies in mood disorders, finding consistently elevated interleukin-6 and cortisol in major depressive disorder and fronto-limbic circuit involvement in both MDD and bipolar disorder. Inflammatory markers decreased and BDNF increased after treatment, though methodological heterogeneity limits comparability.

papers.title: Enantiomer-specific modulation of GABAA receptors differentially regulates stress-induced dopamine dysregulation.
papers.summary: Using an acute footshock stress model and in vivo electrophysiology, this study compared three structurally related GABAA receptor PAMs with distinct α-subunit selectivity. The selective α5-GABAAR PAM MP-III-022 and the α5-preferring enantiomer GL-II-73 normalized stress-induced elevations in VTA dopamine neuron activity, whereas the α2/α3-preferring PAM GL-I-54 did not.

papers.title: X-linked ichthyosis with seizures, ADHD, and autism spectrum disorder: a case report with an uncommon clinical presentation.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 10-year-old boy with X-linked ichthyosis, seizures, ADHD, and autism spectrum disorder, found to have a 1.65 Mb deletion on Xp22.31 including the STS gene and low STS enzyme activity. The authors emphasize early genetic diagnosis and multidisciplinary care for emerging neurodevelopmental and psychiatric features.

papers.title: Ambulatory Surgery Centers in Cardiac Electrophysiology: Current Status and Future Directions.
papers.summary: This review discusses the current status and future directions of ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) in cardiac electrophysiology. It reports that ASCs provide comparable safety, effectiveness, and efficiency to hospital settings for elective EP procedures, but highlights regulatory barriers, insurance variability, and the need for standardized registries.

papers.title: Evaluating and comparing the signalling and functional landscape of hiPSC-CMs derived from patients with dilated cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: Generated hiPSC-CMs from two healthy controls and two dilated cardiomyopathy patients and profiled patient-specific GPCR signaling using PKA and ERK biosensors plus calcium handling, contractility, and electrophysiology. The pipeline revealed altered molecular signaling and functional signatures in DCM lines, providing a platform for personalized mechanism discovery and treatment development.

papers.title: Intraosseous venous malformation of the clivus.
papers.summary: Reported a teenage patient with intermittent right tongue numbness and twitching caused by an expansile clival mass, diagnosed by trans-sphenoidal biopsy as an intraosseous venous malformation (cavernous type). After empirical propranolol therapy for 2 years, the patient became asymptomatic with slight lesion reduction and subsequent stability.

papers.title: Radiomics analysis of dual-layer spectral detector CT-derived iodine density maps for predicting the pathological complete response of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.
papers.summary: Developed radiomics models from dual-layer spectral detector CT iodine density maps combined with clinicopathological and spectral parameters to predict pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in 129 esophageal squamous cell carcinoma patients. The combined model achieved AUCs of 0.943 in training and 0.833 in validation, identifying differentiation grade, venous-phase normalized iodine density, and Radscore as independent predictors.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
